10| On queues
11| ---------
12| 
13| The queue on the GLObject can be associated with other queues. These
14| can be queues of other gloo objects, or of the canvas.context. Queues that are
15| associated behave as if they are a single queue; this allows GL commands for
16| two or more interdependent GL objects to be combined such that they are always
17| sent to the same context together.
18| 
19| A program associates the textures/buffers when they are set via __setitem__. A
20| FrameBuffer does so when assigning buffers. A program associates itself
21| with the canvas.context in draw(). A FrameBuffer does the same in
22| activate().
23| 
24| Example:
25| 
26|     prog1, prog2 = Program(), Program()
27|     tex1, tex2 = Texture(), Texture()
28| 
29|     prog1.glir.associate(tex1.glir)  # prog1 and tex1 now share a queue
30|     prog2.glir.associate(tex2.glir)  # prog2 and tex2 now share a queue
31| 
32|     # this causes prog1, tex1, and canvas.context to all share a queue:
33|     canvas.context.glir.associate(prog1.glir)
34|     # and now all objects share a single queue
35|     canvas.context.glir.associate(prog2.glir)
36|  
37| Now, when the canvas flushes its queue, it takes all the pending commands
38| from prog1, prog2, tex1, and tex2. 
39| """

44| class GLObject(object):
45|     """ Generic GL object that represents an object on the GPU.
46|     
47|     When a GLObject is instantiated, it is associated with the currently
48|     active Canvas, or with the next Canvas to be created if there is
49|     no current Canvas
50|     """
51|     
52|     # Type of GLIR object, reset in subclasses
53|     _GLIR_TYPE = 'DummyGlirType'
54|     
55|     # Internal id counter to keep track of GPU objects
56|     _idcount = 0
57|     
58|     def __init__(self):
59|         """ Initialize the object in the default state """
60|         
61|         # Give this object an id
62|         GLObject._idcount += 1
63|         self._id = GLObject._idcount
64|         
65|         # Create the GLIR queue in which we queue our commands. 
66|         # See docs above for details.
67|         self._glir = GlirQueue()
68|         
69|         # Give glir command to create GL representation of this object
70|         self._glir.command('CREATE', self._id, self._GLIR_TYPE)
71|     
72|     def __del__(self):
73|         # You never know when this is goint to happen. The window might
74|         # already be closed and no OpenGL context might be available.
75|         # However, since we are using GLIR queue, this does not matter!
76|         # If the command gets transported to the canvas, that is great,
77|         # if not, this probably means that the canvas no longer exists.
78|         self.delete()
79| 
80|     def delete(self):
81|         """ Delete the object from GPU memory. 
82| 
83|         Note that the GPU object will also be deleted when this gloo
84|         object is about to be deleted. However, sometimes you want to
85|         explicitly delete the GPU object explicitly.
86|         """
87|         # We only allow the object from being deleted once, otherwise
88|         # we might be deleting another GPU object that got our gl-id
89|         # after our GPU object was deleted. Also note that e.g.
90|         # DataBufferView does not have the _glir attribute.
91|         if hasattr(self, '_glir'):
92|             # Send our final command into the queue
93|             self._glir.command('DELETE', self._id)
94|             # Tell master glir queue that this queue is no longer being used
95|             self._glir._deletable = True
96|             # Detach the queue
97|             del self._glir
